transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time for this pre-purchase review. As you know, we're considering the vendor's indoor-air-quality monitoring system for the science wing. We've been focusing on the six-monitor package at $3,100, but I'd like to hear everyone's findings before I make a final decision. Per our purchasing policy, we'll go in order: facilities manager first, then business office manager, then school nurse. Let's get started.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share my inspection findings before we go further. I completed a room-by-room inspection of the science wing this week, and I found nine separate classrooms that each need a monitor because they have independent ventilation zones. The report hasn't been entered into the purchasing worksheet yet, but based on my inspection, the six-monitor package would leave three classrooms unmonitored. We should be looking at the nine-monitor package instead.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Bell. That's very helpful context for my findings. I can confirm that I verified the restricted capital account ledger this week, and it has exactly enough approved funding to cover the $4,320 nine-monitor package. No general-fund transfer would be needed. The finance memo is ready and awaiting this pre-purchase review for final documentation.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I've completed my review of the student health plans this week. My findings show that the monitors' alerts must be set at 1,000 ppm carbon dioxide, and I need to review the alerts weekly during the first quarter.
